Automate Verse with Zapier#

Status: the app is validated against the Zapier platform schema and zapier validate (local), and its triggers and actions are exercised against a mock server — it is not yet published to Zapier's app directory. Until it is, it runs as a private integration you are invited to; the source is integrations/automation/zapier/ in the repo.

When a scene finishes compiling, a client pins a review comment, or a compile fails, Zapier can post to Slack, drop a row in a sheet, or mail the share link — without any code on your side. Going the other way, a Zap can hand Verse a file link from Dropbox or Drive and get a scene back.

You need: a Verse account token (see Share privately with tokens) and a Zapier account.

1. Connect your account#

Add the Verse Engine app to a Zap. Zapier asks for two things:

  • Verse server — the origin your account lives on (prefilled with the public host; self-hosters paste their own).
  • Account token — the 64-hex token from POST /v1/account or /studio.

Zapier tests the connection with GET /v1/account and labels it with your account name.

2. Triggers and actions#

NameWhat it does
TriggerNew Scene ReadyFires when an upload you own finishes: job (the scene id), url (the share link), vpkUrl.
TriggerScene FailedFires when a compile fails: job, the friendly error and its code.
TriggerNew Review CommentFires when a reviewer pins a comment: scene, comment.text, comment.author, comment.pos.
ActionUpload Model From URLHands Verse a public file link (GLB, IFC, USD, FBX/OBJ zip, splat, point cloud); returns the job id and the share link it will have.
ActionCreate Share LinkMints a tokened link for a scene you own — what opens a private scene.
SearchGet Scene AnalyticsViews, unique viewers, time spent, funnel and rooms over the last 7, 30 or 90 days.

The triggers are instant: turning a Zap on registers a webhook on your account (POST /v1/account/webhooks, one event each); turning it off deletes it. Nothing polls.

3. Worked example: new scene → Slack#

  1. Trigger: Verse Engine → New Scene Ready. Zapier loads your existing scenes as sample data so you can map fields before the first real upload.
  2. Action: Slack → Send Channel Message. Message:
    Code
    New scene ready: {{job}}
{{url}}
  3. Turn the Zap on. The next upload you own (from /app, the Blender add-on, or the action below) posts its link the moment the compile finishes.

4. Worked example: Dropbox file → Verse scene#

  1. Trigger: Dropbox → New File in Folder (a publish/ folder).
  2. Action: Verse Engine → Upload Model From URL. File URL: Dropbox's Direct Media Link (or a shared link with dl=1). **Scene name:** the file name without extension.
  3. The action returns job; the scene is live when a New Scene Ready Zap fires for it, or when GET /v1/ingest/<job> says status: done.

Uploads count against your account's ingest rate (20 per hour per token) and the same 512 MB cap as a direct upload; the server fetches the file itself, so the link must be public and direct.

The same thing over HTTP#

Everything the app does is a documented call: subscribe with POST /v1/account/webhooks, upload with POST /v1/ingest/url { "url": "https://…/model.glb", "name": "flat" }, mint a link with POST /v1/scenes/<id>/share. A Zapier Webhooks by Zapier step can do the same if you prefer not to wait for the directory listing.
